title: Captain Matthew's two recorded marriages: Abigail Dyer first, Clarissa Cobb second
type: Kinship explicitly reported in near-contemporary local histories
finding: The 1865 Eaton Thomaston/Rockland family register explicitly lists Capt. Matthew Beverage of Hope as husband of Abigail Dyer FIRST and Clarissa Cobb SECOND, with five named children by each wife. Eaton's earlier 1851 Annals of Warren independently within his own writings identifies Clarissa as Capt. Barnabas Cobb's daughter and Capt. Matthew's wife. The Colony (2016) reports a Matthew/Abigail wedding in 1801. These written accounts are consistent on the first-wife name; the published second-wife entry is not a contradictory Matthew identity by itself.
limitations: Eaton's 1851 and 1865 writings are two accounts by the SAME AUTHOR, not independent original marriage returns. The 2016 family book does not independently identify the earlier 1785 minor or prove that Capt. Matthew of Hope was Thomas Beverage's brother. Eaton's list gives wives in order but no original marriage dates, complete parentage or authenticated estate. Do not create a new parental edge from this printed household alone.

title: Nathaniel Beverage and Sarah Alexander: two recorded links to Capt. Matthew
finding: Eaton's 1865 Thomaston/Rockland account describes Nathaniel Beverage, born about 1804, as a nephew of Capt. Matthew and describes Nathaniel's wife Sarah Alexander as a niece of the same captain. The paragraph names children Henry T., Mercy and Frederic and Nathaniel as a carpenter living in Rockland after Fox Islands.
limitations: The 1865 narrator gives no names for either nephew's parent or Sarah's parent. 'Niece of ditto' refers to Captain Matthew, not to Nathaniel. The word nephew does not identify which parental sibling of Matthew was Nathaniel's parent, and relationship could reflect affinal usage. The secondary entry is not two proofs because it names two relatives in one account.

title: Original Topsham surveys: 1760, June 1763, and April 1764
named_people: Samuel Beveridge in the published settlers' map key
finding: Maine Historical Society catalogs three genuine Pejepscot manuscript maps: circa 1760 Coll.61 Map 33, a large June 28 1763 survey Coll.61 Map 77 (121 × 146 cm) listing numbered lots and multiple early Topsham settlers, and an April 7 1764 map Coll.61 Map 40. The 1763 survey precedes the December 21 1763 petition printed with James Beveridge's name and supplies dated land-geography context for the 1758 lot-7 research lead.
limitations: The 1763 map's PUBLIC CATALOG description lists selected landowners but does not name Beveridge. We have NOT identified a Beveridge label, verified lot 7, inspected a land conveyance, or established that the 1724 Marblehead James was the 1763 petitioner. Map 77's full size may require permissions for a usable high-resolution copy; do not copy restricted archival images to our site.

title: Who were Nathaniel's parents? Do not confuse an online tree with an original birth
finding: A collaborative compiled New England genealogy assigns the Nathaniel who married Sarah Alexander to parents John White Beverage and Rachel Crosby. The 1865 Eaton history identifies Nathaniel as Captain Matthew's nephew but does not state his parents. These are compatible only if a relevant relationship bridge is documented; treating the web tree as a birth certificate would be circular.
limitations: No original baptism, probate or family register naming Nathaniel's birth parents has been inspected. The existence of another Nathaniel Winslow Beverage (1776) increases risk of accidental merging; the exact date 20 Oct 1803 is a derivative lead only.
